decisions.statement: One page's edits are worked out over one reading of that page's body.
A key put in lands after the key named, and last where no key is named.
A key put in the place of another takes that other key's whole property.
A key the page states already is refused rather than stated twice.
A key the page states nowhere is dropped by nothing rather than refused.
A value put into a list falls after the values that list holds, whatever order they are in.
A key the page states nowhere gains that value as its one value in a list.
A value the list holds already is refused rather than held twice.
A key holding one value rather than a list is refused as a restatement.
The first of the values named that a list holds is the one that goes.
A list holding none of the values named is refused by its key.
A record the list holds already is refused rather than held twice.
The record that goes is the one stating the text named under the field named.
A key more than one record of which states that text is refused.
A key stating no record is refused rather than answered as no edit.
A page exporting no object is refused by its path.
Edits touching one passage of a page come out as one edit over that passage.
One page refused refuses the whole run, and the refusal names that page.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here says which pages are written.

definition: the edits writing a page's properties, their values and the records they hold
